newsitem.title: USA: FBI backs Canada handling of Saudi bomb case.
newsitem.headline: FBI backs Canada handling of Saudi bomb case.

text.p: The Federal Bureau of Investigation said on Saturday it was satisfied with Canada's handling of a Saudi dissident in connection with last June's bombing that killed 19 U.S. airmen in Saudi Arabia.

The FBI said in a statement there had been erroneous press reports that the law enforcement agency was frustrated by the timing of the arrest of Hani Abdel-Rahim Hussein al-Sayegh by Canadian authorities.
"The FBI is fully satisfied with the conduct of the investigation by the Candians, the timing of the arrest, and the high degree of cooperation afforded to U.S. authorities," the statement said.
"The FBI will seek authority to interview al-Sayegh at the conclusion of the legal proceeding in Canada," the FBI said.
The 28-year-old Shiite Moslem was arrested in Ottawa last month. Sayegh denies any role in the bombing and has said he was in Syria last June.
He arrived in Canada applying for refugee status from Saudi Arabia because of what he said was the way the Sunni Moslem rulers treated Shiites.
